questions.q: What is the main motivation for multi-model serving?
options: To make every model run slower on purpose
To share GPU capacity across many models instead of dedicating an underused GPU pool to each one
To avoid ever needing more than one GPU in a company
To eliminate the need for load balancing
questions.explain: Dedicating a GPU pool to every model is simple but wasteful since most models don't fully use their pinned capacity most of the time. Multiplexing shares that capacity across models.

questions.q: What distinguishes full model multiplexing from LoRA adapter multiplexing?
options: There is no difference; both terms describe the same technique
Full model multiplexing serves genuinely distinct models each with their own weights; LoRA multiplexing serves many fine-tuned variants of one shared base model
LoRA adapters can only be used for image models
Full model multiplexing requires no GPU memory at all
questions.explain: Full multiplexing (e.g., a Triton model repository) loads distinct models side by side, each with its own full weights. LoRA multiplexing shares one base model's weights and swaps small adapters per request.

questions.q: Why is LoRA adapter multiplexing dramatically cheaper for serving many per-tenant fine-tuned variants?
options: Because adapters are typically tens to a few hundred megabytes, versus the full gigabytes a separate model would need, while the base weights load only once
Because LoRA adapters eliminate the need for a GPU entirely
Because LoRA adapters are only used for training, never for serving
Because each adapter requires its own dedicated server
questions.explain: LoRA adapters are small relative to full model weights, and the shared base model is loaded only once, so adding another tenant's variant costs megabytes rather than a whole new model's footprint.

questions.q: In the example vLLM command, what does `--lora-modules customer-a=... customer-b=...` do?
options: It deletes the base model after loading
It registers two named LoRA adapters that can be selected per request on top of the shared base model
It forces every request to use both adapters simultaneously
It disables GPU memory sharing
questions.explain: This flag loads named adapters alongside the base model; a request specifies which one it wants applied, letting many tenants share one base model's loaded weights.

questions.q: Why does isolation (resource quotas, priority tiers) still matter in multi-model serving even though sharing raises utilization?
options: Because without limits, one model's traffic spike or bug can starve or disrupt other models sharing the same GPU
Isolation is purely a legal requirement with no technical purpose
Because GPUs automatically isolate every process with zero configuration
Priority tiers are only relevant for CPU-based services, not GPU serving
questions.explain: Shared GPU capacity means contention: a quota caps how much any one model can claim, and priority tiers keep a lower-priority model's heavy load from blocking higher-priority traffic.
